text.p: - Slovenia's conservative People's Party said on Monday it was considering forming a coalition with the leading centre-left Liberal Democrats of prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek.
- An unidentified man of about 25 robbed a jewellery store in Celje 73 km (44.5 miles) east of Ljubljana on Monday.
- Slovenian President Milan Kucan and Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek on Monday met a delegation of Finnland's parliament.

- President of centre-left Liberal Democrats Janez Drnovsek and president of former communist party, United list of Social Democrats Janez Kocijancic met on Monday to discuss future cooperation between the two parties.
- Slovenia's December inflation rose by 0.7 percent, the country's statistical office said.
- In 1996 Renault had the biggest market share of Slovenia's car market with 26.3 percent, followed by Volkswagen with 11.1 percent and Hyundai in third place with 7.4 percent of the market.
- Damage to Ljubljana's electricity system caused by snow and ice on power-lines looks likely to exceed two billion tolars ($13.9 million), electricity distributors said.
- The City of Ljubljana will buy 21 new buses by the summer. The investment will cost some 900 million tolars.
